rules.sentence: Like other soft-tissue sarcomas (STS), surgical resection (to achieve microscopic negative margins) along with perioperative radiotherapy remains the cornerstone of treatment.
The role of neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy remains controversial in adults but is utilized regularly in the pediatric population.
The translocation between the SS18 gene on chromosome 18 and one of the several synovial sarcoma X (SSX) genes on chromosome X is reported in more than 90% of patients.
Radiation-induced synovial sarcoma is an extremely rare entity but has been described in the literature.[2]
